verdict.line: You lose if you stand and trade autos while Camille stacks Adaptive Defenses off her Q/W pokes into a level-6 Hextech Ultimatum cage; you win if you dash through her E (Hookshot) instead of tanking it and punish the cooldown window that follows.

brief.thesis: Camille's entire kit is built around her E (Hookshot) as both engage and reset tool, and Aatrox's E (Umbral Dash) is one of the cleanest answers in the game to it - dodge or interrupt the hook and she has no follow-up. That structural fact plus Aatrox's stated 50.3% head-to-head over 517 games and measured solo-kill edge means this reads as close in a straight stat-check but tilts your way once you play the E-vs-E interaction correctly and hit your Eclipse spike.

theirWindow.when: she lands E (Hookshot) onto you or a wall
theirWindow.what: She chains auto-reset Q (Precision Protocol) into W (Tactical Sweep) and racks up her Adaptive Defenses shield off each ability hit. Do not stand and trade autos through this - reposition with your own E immediately instead of matching blade for blade.

yourWindow.what: With no gap-close or disengage up, shove hard with your Q (Darkin Blade) chain and look for the all-in - this is where the measured solo-kill advantage actually lives.

start.why: Measured at 51.5% over 196 games, and its per-hit damage block directly blunts Camille's Q/W poke pattern that she uses to farm Adaptive Defenses stacks on you before level 6.

boots.why: 83.7% pick rate and 49.3% win rate; Camille's damage is almost entirely auto-attack based (Q reset, E follow-up autos), so flat physical reduction matters more here than tenacity.

core.why: The proc shield absorbs a chunk of her Q+W all-in burst while its bonus damage matches the trade math of your Q chain - the 60% win-rate path builds this first.
Ability haste compounds your Q (Darkin Blade) charge uptime, letting you re-engage faster than she can reset off a fresh E cooldown.
Converts your sustained-fight damage into healing, which is what actually flips a close 50.3% matchup once fights go past the first exchange.

situational.when: you're ahead and need the dash-reset to run down a fleeing Camille
the rest of their team stacks armor and you need shred in teamfights
you fell behind and need the on-hit healing proc more than Shojin's haste
the enemy team has real hard crowd control beyond Camille's kit

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror's stacking heal answers Camille's true-damage poke and burst-shield playstyle directly, and it rewards the extended all-ins this matchup produces once you commit through her E.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most run (73.3% pick) and highest win-rate (50.9%) combo, and it converts your measured solo-kill advantage into actual kills once you punish her E cooldown. Flash+Teleport (45.9%, 25% pick) is the alternative if you'd rather play the wave and scale.

playing.title: Dash through her E, not into it
playing.detail: Use E (Umbral Dash) reactively to sidestep where Camille's Hookshot lands once she gets it around level 3-4, denying the free auto-reset and passive shield stack that follow a landed hook.

playing.title: Punish the E cooldown window
playing.detail: The moment she uses E to reposition or escape, shove immediately with your Q (Darkin Blade) chain - she has no gap-close until it's back, which is exactly where the solo-kill edge lives.

playing.title: Trade spells, not autos
playing.detail: Every ability she lands grants a stacking Adaptive Defenses shield, so land your Q hits and R-empowered autos on your terms instead of standing in extended auto-attack exchanges she wins.

playing.title: Don't fight her lvl2-3 spike unbuilt
playing.detail: Her double-ability Q+W combo out-trades your single maxed Q before level 4; hold W (Infernal Chains) for peel and avoid initiating first in this window.

playing.title: Match ults before committing at 6
playing.detail: If she has R (Hextech Ultimatum) up and you don't, disengage. Once your own R (World Ender) is up, its extended E range and healing let you walk through her cage and punish the commit.

playing.title: Rush Eclipse before extended trades
playing.detail: The highest win-rate path completes Eclipse first; its proc shield is what actually survives her burst math, so avoid drawn-out exchanges before the component pieces are online.

playing.title: Track wall availability on her hook angle
playing.detail: Her E needs a wall or champion to grapple to - if there's no wall in range during a chase, she has no way to reset onto you.

brief.patchCaveat: All win rates, sample sizes, item paths, runes, and summoner splits above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning tying them together - the E-vs-E interaction, the cooldown-window punish, the shield-denial trading pattern - is my own tactical read, not something OP.GG measures directly.
